newsitem.title: UK: Rifkind backs UK's Clarke as chancellor.
newsitem.headline: Rifkind backs UK's Clarke as chancellor.

text.p: Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said on Sunday it was in Britain's national interest that Kenneth Clarke remain as Chancellor of the Exchequer.

A bitter dispute within the ruling Conservative Party over relations with Europe and Britain's policy over a single currency has led to some Conservative members of parliament to call for Clarke to be sacked.
"It's very much in the national interest that he remain chancellor," Rifkind said on the BBC's Breakfast with Frost programme.
He said Clarke had presided over "splendid economic progress".
"There is no doubt that the United Kingdom has the strongest economy in Western Europe," Rifkind added.

Rifkind defended the government's "wait and see" policy on a single European currency, saying a decision on whether to join had to be taken on the basis of the national interest and "there is no national benefit in forcing a decisin now".
The Foreign Secretary criticised "Eurosceptic" Conservative members of parliament, saying they were damaging the party in the run-up to a general election which must be held by next May 22.
"I don't believe they represent the will of the Conservative Party as a whole," Rifkind said.

Prime Minister John Major, in a television interview on Sunday, was expected to make a personal bid to stop support haemmorhaging from a government clinging precariously to office after a week of bitter internal feuding over Europe.
